title: Conservative neural posterior estimation via distributionally robust training
claim: Under limited simulation budgets, standard posterior estimators are overconfident and miss the true parameter, while a robust objective gives wider, covering posteriors.
layout: 1 panel, 2-D contour plot with true-parameter marker and legend
description: A single square plot of overlaid 2-D kernel-density contour lines over parameters theta_1 (x axis, 0.7 to 1.0) and theta_2 (y axis, 0.015 to 0.040). Three sets of contours appear. A tight blue cluster in the lower left is narrow and sits away from the truth, which looks like an overconfident baseline. A broad green set of contours is wide and covers the true parameter. A grey set of contours sits near the center and around the true parameter. A black X marks the true theta, and a legend box in the lower right explains it. The contours overlap heavily. The eye goes first to the black X and the contrast between the small blue blob and the large green region. There is no title, and the figure has no legend for the colors.
caption: Lotka--Volterra posteriors in a low-simulation regime; details in [ref].
abstract: Simulation-based inference with neural posterior estimation (NPE) often yields overconfident and unreliable posteriors under limited simulation budgets. To address this, we propose DRO-NPE, a distributionally robust approach that replaces the standard NPE objective with a worst-case loss over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. We introduce KL-based metrics for miscoverage and miscalibration, and use these to show that the DRO-NPE objective controls overfitting and reduces posterior overconfidence. Our method is tractable, parallelisable, and readily integrates with standard normalising flows. Across benchmark SBI tasks, DRO-NPE consistently improves coverage and calibration, while narrowing the gap between empirical and population NPE loss, leading to more reliable inference in low-simulation regimes.
